question: What is the main hormone behind most skin changes during pregnancy?
explanation: You've got this! High levels of pregnancy hormones like estrogen and progesterone wake up pigment cells and blood vessels in the skin. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h1)

question: Why do most pregnancy skin changes need no medical treatment?

options.A: Maternal skin becomes completely immune to disease
options.B: The placenta blocks all medications from working
options.C: Hormones stop circulating after the first trimester
options.D: They are normal body responses that fade after delivery

explanation: No stress here! Changes like darkening skin are just harmless body responses to pregnancy hormones that naturally get better after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h1)

question: What is the dark vertical line that often appears on a pregnant belly called?
explanation: Great job! Linea nigra simply means 'black line' in Latin—it's that common dark stripe that shows up on the tummy due to extra skin pigment. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: A pregnant patient asks how to reduce dark patches on her face. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Scrub the face vigorously with harsh soap twice a day
options.B: Stop drinking milk immediately to clear skin pigment
options.C: Apply strong bleaching creams prescribed over the counter
options.D: Apply daily sunscreen and wear wide-brimmed hats outdoors

explanation: Sunlight makes facial darkening (melasma) pop out more. Advising sun protection is a simple, effective tip every nursing student should know! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: What causes stretch marks, or striae gravidarum, during pregnancy?

options.A: Fungal infections growing under tight clothing
options.B: Blockage of sweat glands by high hormone levels
options.C: Accumulation of excess subcutaneous fat deposits
options.D: Breaking of elastic fibers in the dermis from rapid stretching

explanation: As the belly grows quickly, the elastic fibers in the deeper skin layer stretch and tiny breaks happen, leading to stretch marks. Completely normal! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h3)

question: Which finding is a normal vascular change expected during a routine prenatal checkup?

options.B: Small spider angiomas on the upper chest
options.C: Painful deep purple nodules on the calves
options.D: Complete absence of blood flow to the fingers

explanation: Spotting small spider-like blood vessels (angiomas) is super common due to extra blood volume and high estrogen during pregnancy. Nothing to worry about! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h3)

question: Why do many women experience sudden hair loss a few months after giving birth?

options.A: Breastfeeding drains all essential proteins from the scalp
options.B: Stored-up hairs from the growth phase shed all at once as hormones drop
options.C: Washing hair too frequently damages the weak hair roots
options.D: Newborn care stress permanently destroys hair follicles

explanation: During pregnancy, thick hormones hold onto your hair. Once those hormones drop after birth, all that extra hair decides to take a break and shed at once! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: What is the term for the normal, temporary hair shedding that happens after childbirth?
explanation: Fancy name, simple meaning! 'Telogen effluvium' just describes that normal phase where hair sheds after delivery before the cycle resets. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: Which symptom is a major red flag for intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy?

options.A: Painful blisters forming exclusively around the mouth
options.B: Rapid darkening of the skin over the entire body
options.C: Severe itching on the palms and soles without an initial rash
options.D: Thick crusting sores spreading across the scalp

explanation: Take note of this one for the ward! Intense itching on hands and feet without a rash can mean liver acid backup (cholestasis) and needs quick medical attention. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h5)

question: Which of these skin conditions needs careful medical evaluation rather than just reassurance?

options.A: Mild palmar erythema on the hands
options.B: Linea nigra across the lower abdomen
options.D: Spider angiomas on the upper chest

explanation: While lines and spider veins are harmless, cholestasis involves the liver and requires close monitoring to keep the baby safe. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h5)

question: What usually happens to stretch marks over time after delivery?

options.A: They fade from reddish-purple to silvery-white lines
options.B: They develop painful open ulcers that require suturing
options.C: They turn dark brown and raise above the skin surface
options.D: They completely disappear without leaving any trace

explanation: Stretch marks start out bright and angry-looking, but over time they calm down and fade into soft, silvery lines. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h6)

question: How does the body get rid of extra fluid from the skin and tissues right after birth?

options.A: Through rapid shedding of the top layer of skin cells
options.B: By reabsorbing all fluid directly back into the digestive tract
options.C: Through heavy postpartum sweating and increased urination
options.D: By storing extra fluid permanently in the muscle tissue

explanation: Sweating buckets and frequent bathroom trips are your body's clever ways of clearing out all that extra pregnancy fluid! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h6)

question: A pregnant woman is worried about dark patches on her face and a line on her belly. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Reassure her that these are normal hormonal changes that usually fade after birth
options.B: Advise her to scrub the dark areas hard with soap every morning
options.C: Explain that these marks indicate a dangerous vitamin deficiency in her diet
options.D: Tell her to immediately see a dermatologist for emergency skin surgery

explanation: A warm, reassuring word goes a long way! Explaining that these marks are normal helps anxious mums relax. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h7)

question: What is a key nursing duty when checking a pregnant patient's skin?

options.A: Differentiating harmless body changes from serious medical conditions
options.B: Telling the patient to ignore any skin changes until after delivery
options.C: Reporting all common stretch marks to the primary surgeon
options.D: Prescribing strong steroid creams to cure all rashes instantly

explanation: You are the frontline! Knowing the difference between normal pregnancy glow-ups and warning signs like cholestasis makes you an awesome nurse. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h7)
